subject: You're sharing your real-time location with Ivana Wu + 1 other
body_text:
Rebecca,

To protect your privacy, this is a reminder that you're sharing your 
real-time location persistently with

* Jeslyn Wu


They can add notifications to know when you arrive at or leave a specific 
location.


Google Location Sharing lets friends and family see your real-time location 
across Google apps, services, and devices like smart displays. You can stop 
sharing at any time in settings. Manage your location: 
https://myaccount.google.com/locationsharing?utm_source=email&utm_medium=plaintext_email_reminder_body&utm_campaign=location_sharing_reminders

subject: Build Smarter Autonomous AI Agents with MongoDB
body_text:
To view this email as a web page, go to the following address: https://info.mongodb.com/index.php/email/emailWebview?mkt_tok=MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSM45T2fMrwYTXjma6MxpjmupXJzTDtqMrhr2md86ZWXk157meNBotHzRb-eeBVAxbvWIU9etIuHfUW5kXyejX8p0m6cqTpeKeKbGoB749vFNQ 

Hi Rebecca,


The fourth session of our series, RAG with MongoDB and Python, is now available to watch on-demand.

Join us for the series finale on April 1 at 11am ET, Agents with MongoDB and 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSM45e5DGOrpH0ZXu09gjR28y9wfwUNgkw-GBaTiDl85-92zqAlz5kd6Tp8zkMwxjzdurg0=>, where we bring everything together to develop autonomous AI agents powered by LangGraph and real-time database orchestration.


	- Learn how to leverage MongoDB for real-time data management and seamless database orchestration to enhance AI agent workflows.
	- Discover how LangGraph simplifies the integration of Python-based autonomous agents with MongoDB to build intelligent, scalable systems.
	- Gain hands-on insights into creating fully functional AI agents equipped for decision-making and adaptability.



MongoDB experts will be available for 1:1 support to help you troubleshoot issues and answer your questions in live time as we go through hands-on challenges. 

Additionally, you’ll have another opportunity to earn a MongoDB Skill Badge during the workshop that you can add to your LinkedIn profile to showcase your expertise in modern data architecture. 

If you want to catch up on Part 4: RAG with MongoDB and 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSM45Fwi9qsr3KAyrpUopZ85atRSfbSVWkeKtlUXn38SrmQEKwTRzsKrKVpAXSlZhWJ3w44=>, the recording is now on-demand. You can also still complete the corresponding Skill 
Badge <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSM45F9uSCpTxYJuBInm-Chi7RtcrvnGjgJC-VPk6jeFrralUwltuuqss6YI5CQrplPQ74s=>.

Ready to start building autonomous AI agents?
Register now <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSM45UjFHe6mgDE1tX6MCFdcyjrCSFcNYyapEo-ml0LTG3iUs2sQbAsf7m3nPEVto3P7cug=>
Think Big, Go Far,
The MongoDB Team

This email was sent to rebecca.choi05@gmail.com. If you no longer wish to receive these emails you may unsubscribe here: https://info.mongodb.com/UnsubscribePage.html?mkt_unsubscribe=1&mkt_tok=MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSM45T2fMrwYTXjma6MxpjmupXJzTDtqMrhr2md86ZWXk157meNBotHzRb-eeBVAxbvWIU9etIuHfUW5kXyejX8p0m6cqTpeKeKbGoB749vFNQ.

Hi Jasmin,


The fourth session of our series, RAG with MongoDB and Python, is now available to watch on-demand.

Join us for the series finale on April 1 at 11am ET, Agents with MongoDB and 
Python <https://em.mongodb.com/MTQ5LUNCSi0xMzYAAAGgxSO8tX1Rj72NWcOBNGlr1GUCKu-EzED5wA1WnE2pRdoIapGPNyBg-Xtea_5-0C15R4xdDlQ=>, where we bring everything together to develop autonomous AI agents powered by LangGraph and real-time database orchestration.


	- Learn how to leverage MongoDB for real-time data management and seamless database orchestration to enhance AI agent workflows.
	- Discover how LangGraph simplifies the integration of Python-based autonomous agents with MongoDB to build intelligent, scalable systems.
	- Gain hands-on insights into creating fully functional AI agents equipped for decision-making and adaptability.



MongoDB experts will be available for 1:1 support to help you troubleshoot issues and answer your questions in live time as we go through hands-on challenges. 

Additionally, you’ll have another opportunity to earn a MongoDB Skill Badge during the workshop that you can add to your LinkedIn profile to showcase your expertise in modern data architecture.

Ready to start building autonomous AI agents?

body_text: Email from Community Servings Support the Teaching Kitchen & Enter to Win a Seat at the Table!     Celebrate Jacques Pépin’s 90th with a French Feast for a Cause Support the Teaching Kitchen & Enter to Win a Table! Join us on Thursday, November 13, for an unforgettable evening honoring the 90th birthday of legendary chef and philanthropist Jacques Pépin and supporting the Teaching Kitchen at Community Servings, a transformative culinary training and job readiness program. Jacques Pépin and the Jacques Pépin Foundation have long supported culinary education and the mission of the Teaching Kitchen. This special dinner directly benefits the program, empowering aspiring chefs with the skills and confidence to build meaningful careers. The Experience Enjoy a French-inspired menu prepared by Teaching Kitchen trainees and graduates under the expert guidance of Chef Eric Spitz. While Jacques Pépin won’t be in attendance, we will celebrate his legacy through timeless dishes crafted in his honor. Menu Highlights Include: Chicken Liver Mousse, toasted baguette, frisée, radicchio, and fennel salad Beef Daube, pomme purée, glazed carrots or Fall Vegetable Risotto French Cheese Course, preserves, dried and pickled fruits, crostini Dessert Course by Teaching Kitchen graduate and Omni Boston Hotel Seaport Pastry Chef Alexa Ortiz JOIN US! Win a Table With Three Guests of Your Choice Each entry is a suggested donation of $50 and enters you into a promotional drawing for one table of four at this exclusive dinner. Four winners will receive this giveaway. However, no donation or purchase is necessary to enter or win. Winners may invite three guests of their choice and enjoy an unforgettable evening of French cuisine and fine wine inspired by Chef Pépin and prepared by Teaching Kitchen trainees and graduates under Chef Eric Spitz. 5 Places You Should Live if You Love to Travel
http://tracker.thediscoverer.com/tc?&i=9&t=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thediscoverer.com%2Fcontents%2F5ca6219c62e1d00004d385b9%2Fclick%3Femail%3Djasmind009%40gmail.com%26partnerCode%3D%26partnerSubcode%3D%26mailCampaignSource%3DTheDiscoverer%26mailCampaignId%3D1108824526%26mailMessageId%3D7650771%26mailSegmentId%3D1012088640%26position%3D1%26autosubscribe%3D%26utm_source%3D%26utm_medium%3D%26utm_campaign%3D1108824526%26utm_content%3D7650771%26utm_term%3D1012088640

I’ve roamed the length and breadth of the globe for work and pleasure, but after racking up well over a hundred countries, I can honestly say there’s no place like home. That said, it would be pretty hard being a travel writer if home wasn’t within striking distance of several international airports, well served by public transport and close to a couple of major motorways. If, like me, your life revolves around your next trip, here are five places to live if you love to travel.

subject: Webinar on 2023 Summer Art Programs
body_text: Dear Ichen Art Academy Community, We are pleased to announce our upcoming webinar on our 2023 Summer Art Programs, which will be held on Thursday, March 23rd at 7:30 PM PST. subject: Check-in Instructions For Your Upcoming Visit To Carnegie Mellon
body_text:
Check-In For Your Campus Visit

Dear Jasmin,

We look forward to your upcoming campus visit.

When you arrive on campus, we highly recommend that you check in for your visit <https://admission.cmu.edu/register/mobile?cmd=checkin&id=6d4a4cec-c5b1-421f-add6-411f146ce3d2> online using a mobile device. Mobile check-in will require access to your device's GPS location, so please ensure that your phone has no GPS location restrictions enabled. Checking in online will expedite your arrival to campus.

Once you've completed your online check-in, please stop by the Welcome Center desk to pick up your guest stickers and any other materials you may need. You may then proceed directly to the event locations noted below.

You're scheduled for the following event(s):



Tuesday, July 5 at 3:00 PM - Campus Tour -Welcome Center, the Tepper building (Ground Floor)



 
Please refer to our campus map <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/campus-map> for the locations of your scheduled events. We encourage you to arrive at the designated locations no more than 15 minutes before the scheduled start time of each event.

We hope you have a valuable visit experience and are able to learn more about our students, faculty, campus life and the city of Pittsburgh. Here are some resources that may be valuable during your visit:

 Traveling to Pittsburgh & Accommodations <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/visit/on-campus-visit-opportunities/pittsburgh-travel-and-accommodations>
 Arriving On Campus - Parking, Maps & Directions <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/visit/on-campus-visit-opportunities/arriving-on-campus>
 Online Campus Map <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/campus-map>
 Dining On Campus <http://apps.studentaffairs.cmu.edu/dining/conceptinfo/?page=listConcepts>

Campus parking is limited, and we're experiencing significant construction on and around campus - please account for this as you plan your travels. If space is available, park in the East Campus Parking Garage (5040 Forbes Avenue, Pittsburgh, PA 15213). Parking rates are detailed on our Parking and Transportation Services website <http://www.cmu.edu/parking/about/index.html>.

Please note that due to security guidelines and space constraints, the Office of Admission isn't able to store any luggage or personal belongings during your visit. We apologize for the inconvenience and ask you to plan accordingly.

It's also important to note that all campus visitors are required to abide by Carnegie Mellon's COVID-19 visitor protocols <http://www.cmu.edu/coronavirus/visitor-protocol/index.html>. Please keep in mind:

 Visitors to Carnegie Mellon's campus are expected to be vaccinated against COVID-19, including a booster when eligible, unless unable to be vaccinated due to disability or strong religious/moral conviction. 
 Facial coverings both indoors and outdoors are recommended for all visitors. Those who are not up-to-date on vaccinations are required to wear facial coverings both indoors and outdoors. 

If you need to cancel your registration, please click here <https://admission.cmu.edu/register/?k=6d4a4cec-c5b1-421f-add6-411f146ce3d2> prior to your scheduled visit date. This'll help us to accommodate as many students and families as possible.

Have questions or prefer to check in in person? Please stop by the Carnegie Mellon University David and Susan Coulter Welcome Center on the first floor of the Tepper building. At the Welcome Center, you'll find informational brochures <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/downloads> related to admission, aid and our colleges/programs, campus maps and other literature. Please enter the Tepper building via the Forbes Avenue entrance across from Hamburg Hall. You can also stop by the Office of Admission on the second floor of Warner Hall during normal business hours <https://www.cmu.edu/admission/contact-us>. 

We look forward to welcoming you to campus!

Best regards,
Office of Admission


Carnegie Mellon University | Office of Admission
5000 Forbes Avenue, Pittsburgh, PA, 15213 | 412.268.2082 | admission@andrew.cmu.edu

subject: [Inferno 16U Johnson] Inferno Softball: Practice jerseys, spirit wear in and Foster City field safety info
body_text:
Good morning Inferno Nation, 

We will pass out the spirit wear apparel today prior to game and players can wear their practice jerseys in scrimmages today. 

Also, remember to bring some food, water for today. Food for break between games.

Coach Craig

Foster City field safety info is below: 

Subject: Safety Guidelines for Upcoming Friendly in Foster City
To: johnsonfam95@att.net <johnsonfam95@att.net>
CC: Anthony Kong <fcysa.president@gmail.com>


Hi Craig,

We are very excited to host you this coming Sunday. If you guys need anything or have any questions before or during, then just let me know.
Location: Sea Cloud Park Field B2 (grass/dirt field), Sea Cloud Drive, Foster City, CA
Game start time: Sunday 4/11 1:00pm and ~2:45pm (10-15 min break between the two games)
We have some major construction on our levee going on, so parking is a little limited at the moment. People can park on Sea Cloud Drive or around the fence. B2 is to the left when you go all the way down Sea Cloud Drive and hit the construction fencing. You can also park in a small lot by the big turf soccer field and walk over to B2 as well.
Face coverings will be required for everyone, but optional for Pitchers and Outfielders (as those two positions are difficult to keep masks on and breathe properly). Outfielders should still keep their masks under their chin (or in their pockets) while playing defense, in case they need to put it on. All batters and catchers will be reminded to keep masks on and the umpire (who has received both his Covid Vaccine shots already) will also remain masked.
- Each team brings 3-4 Game balls (High School approved Wilsons if you have them), and we’ll switch balls out every half inning, so each  defensive half, that team will only touch their own softballs
- We won’t use the dugouts for players. Players (and only Players and Coaches) can sit on the Bleachers
- Coaches (and scorekeepers) must have face coverings on at all times and may use the dugout, if desired.
- No post game handshakes
- Spectators can bring chairs and sit socially distant (unless same family) beyond the outfield outside the HR fence or along the Foul line off the field of play (starting where OF grass begins). Please ask families not to sit in the scorers box behind the backstop or anywhere near where the players sit. They will be asked to move, if they are there. Again, the outfield foul lines (off the field of play) or beyond the outfield fence is where they should sit.
- Anyone with any kind of fever or not feeling well should stay home
We have a playground by our field that’s open, so siblings can take advantage of that. Also, families should follow face covering and social distancing guidelines.
Bathrooms are open and well maintained, but players are discouraged to use water fountains unless absolutely necessary.
If you haven't been to Foster City in a while, we have various supermarkets and fast food takeout places minutes away from the field, if anyone needs to get food.

I’ve roamed the length and breadth of the globe for work and pleasure, but after racking up well over a hundred countries, I can honestly say there’s no place like home. That said, it would be pretty hard being a travel writer if home wasn’t within striking distance of several international airports, well served by public transport and close to a couple of major motorways. If, like me, your life revolves around your next trip, here are five places to live if you love to travel.

body_text:

---------- Forwarded message ---------
From: HHS NCHS <hhsnchs@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, Sep 22, 2019 at 8:49 AM
Subject: First Meeting Summary
To: Alison Lee <allisonbooks2002@gmail.com>, Coline Luo <
cluo497@student.fuhsd.org>, Emily Yao <ted.bearington888@gmail.com>, Julia
Lou <jlou@sonic.net>, Ryan Miao <ryanmiao.edu@gmail.com>, Vivian Hsia <
hsialiechaplin@gmail.com>, HHS NCHS <hhsnchs@gmail.com>


大家好，

Thank you for attending our first NCHS meeting. Here is a summary of our
meeting along with the slides:

*General Information*
NCHS is part of a nationally recognized scholastic organization. We seek to
spread awareness about Chinese culture and tradition through socials,
volunteering opportunities, and school-wide events. We also recognize
dedicated members who are actively trying to understand Chinese culture.

*How to Get a Cord*
We award our own cord to honor our senior members when they graduate.
Listed in the table on the presentation slides are the requirements that
seniors must fulfill *by the time they graduate* in order to receive a cord.
(If you have never taken a Chinese class at Homestead but have learned
Chinese in a classroom setting somewhere else, feel free to describe your
situation on the application)

*Hours*
To fulfill their hour requirement, NCHS members are expected to attend some
of our socials and participate in the volunteer opportunities that we
offer. If you fall short of 8 hours by the end of the year, we will not
count that school year as a complete year of membership.

*Attendance*
NCHS will hold a meeting once every month on a Friday brunch.
Regardless, *all club members are required to come to meetings*. If you are
unable to come to a meeting, please send an email, including your name and
ID number, to this address notifying us about your absence *at least 24
hours prior* to the meeting. Skipping *three* meetings without prior
notification will result in *immediate expulsion* from the club.
>From this point forward, we will be taking attendance in all of our
meetings.

*NCHS Application*
You must fill out a simple questionnaire in order to be considered for
membership. Complete the attached Google form before the deadline. Then
turn in the $10 donation (preferably cash), if you are able to, to the
orange folder in L112. There will be designated envelopes next to the
folder for you to write your name, student ID, and insert the money.

*We encourage you to apply*. Even if we do not accept your application, you
can try again next year. In the meantime, you will still receive
notifications for any of our events, only that the hours you participate in
for that year do not count towards earning a cord.

All applications are due by *Friday 10/4 at 11:59 PM*.

We look forward to seeing your applications! Please email us any questions
that you have.

*HHS NCHS*

*Vice President: *Vivian Hsia
*Secretary/Treasurer:* Coline Luo
*Volunteering Directors: *Ryan Miao & Julia Lou
*Cultural Director: *Allison Lee

subject: Reminder Upcoming Art Contest DEADLINE
body_text: Dear Ichen Art Academy Community, This is a reminder that deadlines for upcoming art contests are quickly approaching. The Youth Art Contest deadline is THIS SUNDAY 10/23. Students of all ages are encouraged to participate. We have created an art contest FAQ , which may be useful to you. Below is the original email we sent out: 1) 2022 National Youth Art Contest: All K-12 students are eligible to participate. There are five groups: · K-G2 · G3-5 · G6-8 · G9-10 · G11-12 Website: http://www.youthart.org/art-contest-2022.html Deadline for submission: 10/23/2022 2) 2023 Scholastic Art Awards - Kids in grades 7-12 (ages 13 and up) This is the nation's longest running, most prestigious recognition program for creative teens. Deadlines vary by region. For the California Bay Area Art Region, the deadline is December 15 . Students need to go to https://www.artandwriting.org/awards/how-to-enter/ , create an account, upload their artwork, and have our teacher sign an entry form, then submit the form and entry fee. Please be advised that students need to select "Ichen Art Academy" or “Ichen Art Academy-Pleasanton” as the “Other Educational Program” in their profiles . This will help promote our school and make it easy to count the total number of awards from our school. For years many students from Ichen Art Academy have won this prestigious award, which counted as their high school achievements and helped their college applications. You can view our award results from 2018 to 2022 here . We strongly recommend all students ages 13 and up to participate in this art contest. Regards, Ichen Wu Principal of Ichen Art Academy This message was sent to jasmind009@gmail.com . Dangerous goods


For safety reasons, dangerous goods must not be packed in checked or

Subject to the provisions of the Montreal Convention and the Warsaw

Notice of liability limitations


The Montreal Convention or the Warsaw Convention system may be applicable
to your journey and these Conventions govern and may limit the liability of
air carriers for death or bodily injury, for loss, delay, or damage to
baggage.


Where the Montreal Convention applies, the limits of liability are as
follows:

 1. There are no financial limits in respect of death or bodily injury of
 passengers.

 1,519 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 1,900; US $2,000) per
 passenger in most cases.
 3. In respect of damage occasioned by delay in the carriage of persons
 6,303 Special Drawing Rights (approximately EUR 7,700; US $8,300) per

Where the Warsaw Convention system applies, the limits of liability are as
follows:

 1. 16,600 Special Drawing Rights with respect to death or bodily injury

*For more information on Special Drawing Rights* and currency exchange
rates, visit the International Monetary Fund <https://www.imf.org/en/Home>

applicable to your journey. If your journey involves carriage by different

limits of liability.

from a higher limit of liability for loss, delay, or damage to baggage by
making a declaration of your baggage value at check-in and paying any
supplementary fee that may apply. Alternatively, if your baggage value
exceeds the applicable limit of liability, you should fully insure it
before you travel.

NOTICE OF OVERBOOKING OF FLIGHTS In the event that a flight is overbooked, no one will be denied a seat until airline personnel first ask for volunteers willing to give up their reservation in exchange for a payment of the airline's choosing. This year's Pi Day celebration boasts some very special guests: Costume Character Elmo and Costume Character Count Von Count from Sesame Street. Costume Character Elmo is just learning about numbers, of course, but Costume Character Count Von Count is a counting expert!
